subject: biology
title: Animal Physiology (HL) Adventure 3: Reproductive hormones
welcome_lead: Today you'll regulate the menstrual cycle with FSH, LH and oestrogen.
meta_desc: Biology HL — reproductive hormones, menstrual cycle, FSH, LH, oestrogen, progesterone, IVF.
final_note: You learned FSH and LH from the pituitary regulate the ovaries; oestrogen and progesterone control the uterus; positive and negative feedback time the cycle.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The 28-day cycle has two phases linked by ovulation:

- Follicular (day 1-14): FSH stimulates follicle to make oestrogen.
- Luteal (day 14-28): corpus luteum makes progesterone.

If no pregnancy, corpus luteum degenerates → progesterone falls → menstruation.

Early: oestrogen negatively feeds back to pituitary.

Just before ovulation, high oestrogen flips to positive feedback → LH surge → ovulation.

After ovulation, progesterone (+ oestrogen) negatively feedbacks → FSH/LH low until cycle restart.

In vitro fertilisation (Edwards + Steptoe, first baby Louise Brown 1978):

1. FSH injections stimulate multiple follicles.
2. hCG triggers ovulation.
3. Eggs collected, fertilised in dish.
4. Embryos transferred to uterus.

Global ethical debate: surplus embryos, screening for disease (PGD), gene editing (CRISPR).
